title: Decompose CI lint launcher; add on-demand toolchain cache and slim prober
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Feedback loops on lint/test failures are dominated by a monolithic CI entrypoint that bootstraps the entire toolchain and runs all linters even for small JS/Go changes. This PR decomposes the lint/test launcher into smaller, target-aware entrypoints, introduces an on-demand toolchain cache that lazily downloads SDKs/toolchains per job, and adds a slim prober to exercise the minimal startup path for fast preflight checks. This reduces cold-start overhead for presubmit lanes and narrows the surface for flaky tool downloads.

What changed: - Split ci/launcher into ci/launcher/core + ci/launcher/runners to separate orchestration from runner implementations. - Add tools/toolchain-cache: a lightweight Go service that provides on-demand tarball fetching, local layer caching, and manifest-aware eviction. - Replace monolithic .github/workflows/lint.yml with staged invocations that call targeted entrypoints; add a fastpath workflow for changed-files-based linting. - Introduce ci/prober/slim-prober.sh used by staged CI to validate startup within 10s; used as a quick health check before heavier integration runs. - Migration scripts: scripts/ci/migrate-launcher.sh to update runner configs and docs/ci/README.md with new dev workflows.

Checklist: - [x] refactor entrypoints and add unit tests for new modules - [x] toolchain cache integration and e2e smoke - [x] fastpath workflow for small changes - [x] migration guide and docs update - [x] load testing the cache on canary infra

Notes: linear items ENG-2345 and ENG-2399 track follow-ups: rollbacks for legacy runners and adding metrics to the cache. This change intentionally keeps backwards-compatible interfaces; the migrate script is opt-in. See docs/ci/README.md for local dev instructions and the RFC link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2345/ci-toolchain-caching-rfc
